summary: Build a bottom-up 1-D table where each entry is computed from a small fixed number of previous entries via a recurrence, avoiding exponential recomputation from naive recursion.
recognize_when: The problem asks for a count, min/max, or yes/no answer that depends on smaller versions of the same problem (e.g. dp[i] depends on dp[i-1], dp[i-2])
A brute-force recursive solution has overlapping subproblems (recomputes the same state repeatedly)
State can be described by a single index into a sequence, like 'ways to reach step i' or 'best result ending at i'
Keywords like 'number of ways', 'minimum cost to reach', or 'maximum sum/product ending here'
The recurrence only needs a constant window of previous states, hinting space can be optimized to O(1)

complexity.notes: One pass filling the table with O(1) work per entry; space can often be reduced to O(1) by keeping only the last few states instead of the full table.

gotchas: Off-by-one errors in table size or base cases (dp array needs n+1 slots to include index n)
Forgetting to handle small edge cases (n = 0 or 1) before the main loop touches dp[i-2]
Applying the recurrence in the wrong order (must fill smaller indices before larger ones depend on them)
